material_findings.passage: Start identity with local accounts plus multi-factor authentication; pilot ships with local accounts and MFA, while the broker is conditional/deferred.
material_findings.original_obligation: O2 mechanism applicability; summer help-desk closure; P6 unfunded integration; $8,000 budget
material_findings.reasoning: The chosen primary is self-hosted Grist Core, but no component is selected to own local passwords, MFA enrollment/reset, recovery, or identity assertions. Official Grist authentication documentation describes external authentication, including getgrist.com and an external proxy. The separate Builder Edition documents username/password through Authelia. Consequently, a detailed recovery checklist is not evidence that the selected Core stack supplies the promised local account/MFA path. An omitted day-one authentication dependency bears directly on summer operation, maintenance effort and the conditional recommendation.
material_findings.qualification: This is an incomplete, unsupported deployment mechanism, not a claim that Grist can never support local accounts. An external proxy/IdP could provide it. No production implementation or successful runtime test was required by the brief; the required investigation is the available governing component and its applicability.

material_findings.passage: A repeat run in the same cycle with the same state-hash sends nothing; each send-record is written before its send so a mid-batch crash reruns without partial duplicates.
material_findings.original_obligation: O2 consequential notifier behavior; O5 coherent handoffs; O6 discriminating crash validation; P3 caregiver delay messages
material_findings.reasoning: A local delivery-log write and an SMTP send are different commits. If the process stops after the pre-send record but before sendMail, the stated same-cycle rule suppresses an unsent notice. If pending rows are retried instead, a stop after SMTP acceptance but before recording success permits a duplicate. RFC 5321 §4.5.3.2.6 and §6.1 explicitly recognize the acceptance/acknowledgement duplicate window; the n8n send operation awaits SMTP sendMail and returns the result without a transaction with the loan log. The described ordering does not establish the asserted crash-safe behavior.
material_findings.qualification: This is a specification/control-flow counterexample grounded in the selected delivery mechanism, not an executed witness. Delivery-status fields alone do not resolve the two crash windows. V3 is correctly labeled proposed; therefore this finding is not VALIDATION_OVERCLAIM.

material_findings.passage: Do not use the community spreadsheet-database path for this constraint without its paid license; only viable for minimization if the license is funded.
material_findings.original_obligation: O1 viable alternatives; O4 exact P2 need-to-know scope; O5 preservation of verifier conditions/options
material_findings.reasoning: Fine-grained controls on one shared NocoDB table are indeed gated and field-edit permissions do not hide fields. That does not make paid fine-grained redaction a necessary condition for every P2 design. Release 0.301.5 makes workspace-level access control available to self-hosted deployments, and role documentation distinguishes access to whole bases/projects from finer row/field controls. The verifier explicitly retained separation, fewer members, or API-side redaction as alternatives (verification.md:74–76). The final acknowledges workspace separation but discounts it because it does not redact rows/columns, even though the original P2 does not require teachers and restricted contacts in the same table/workspace. It loses the compatible separation option while reporting Q1 as wholly strengthening the rejection.
material_findings.qualification: The verifier is also fallible: its specific Private Project suggestion is paid under current Private Project Availability (Business+), so that particular option cannot be credited as a proven free feature. The supported narrower option is separation by permitted workspace/base access or an independently verified redacting API; no claim is made that such a deployment has already passed privacy tests or is cheapest.

material_findings.passage: Downtime in minutes at entry and hours in analysis where that product is used; mixed units are a defect.
material_findings.original_obligation: O2 governing units/types and domain applicability for ERPNext Asset Repair; O5 preservation of correct qualifications
material_findings.reasoning: The minutes-entry/hours-report documentation is explicitly Home > Manufacturing > Production/Reports and concerns machine Downtime Entry/Analysis. The investigated repair mechanism is Asset Repair. Both pinned Asset Repair implementations use get_downtime() with time_diff_in_hours; both schemas make downtime a read-only Data field. Applying the Manufacturing entry rule to instrument Asset Repair is a domain error. The critic explicitly preserved it without re-verifying, and the final carries it forward as a governing unit rule.
material_findings.qualification: The Manufacturing statement is correct in its own domain. This finding is confined to its application to the selected Asset Repair alternative; it does not contradict the correct days/calendar-date rules or claim an actual factor-60 runtime error was observed. A proposed later unit check does not ground the current assertion.

material_findings.passage: Expected return is an indexed nullable date, not text; date-vs-datetime and null-means-no-deadline fixed in the schema.
material_findings.original_obligation: O2 governing field types/defaults and applicability for the viable PocketBase core; P1 expected return; O6 no-deadline/overdue oracle
material_findings.reasoning: The final carries PocketBase as a viable core and cites its collections page, but does not investigate the governing type mismatch for its central expected-return requirement. PocketBase Fields specifies non-nullable fields except JSONField, zero-default fallbacks, and a DateField storing a datetime string with empty-string default and full-string comparisons. The final supplies a platform-neutral nullable calendar-DATE rule without identifying this native behavior or qualifying how absent deadlines and school-local date boundaries apply on the PocketBase branch. Applying the written overdue comparison directly to the native default can classify an empty deadline as before today.
material_findings.qualification: The desired nullable calendar-date business semantics are reasonable. This is not proof that they cannot be implemented or a demand for a complete adapter. It is an omitted, available consequential type/default investigation on a retained alternative; the other cores are not asserted to share this defect.

material_findings.passage: Per-seat SaaS is rejected for the pilot on recurring seat cost plus data-residency review against $8k and unfunded integration.
material_findings.original_obligation: O1 materially different viable approaches; O2 consequential cost/applicability; O4 inappropriate rejection; original $8,000 budget and unfunded formal integration
material_findings.reasoning: The final rejects the per-seat hosted category without a named priced candidate, teacher/paid-seat count, district residency rule, or integration requirement establishing the rejection. The brief supplies a budget and an unfunded integration request, not a ban on subscription hosting. Official Grist pricing demonstrates that per-seat hosted products have concrete modest starting prices ($8 annual/$10 monthly Pro per user); those prices alone do not establish a district fit, but they defeat recurring-seat cost as an inherent incompatibility. Official Lend-Engine pricing separately demonstrates a lending-native hosted category worth conditionally assessing. The final makes a stronger conclusion than its evidence supports.
material_findings.qualification: This assessment does not infer the district has 20 teachers, approve any vendor, or declare a hosted product fully compliant. A self-hosted preference could be reasonable. The defect is a categorical consequential rejection on uninvestigated cost/policy assumptions, not failure to discover one particular product.

method_clues.blinding: Partial only: exact input map exposes actual_arm; paths and stage assignments expose M15 and the treatment verifier context. These clues were unavoidable and disclosed; not a blinded comparison.
method_clues.candidate_method: Control investigator/full critic/full reviser; treatment additionally has three neutral verification questions and independent verifier package. Neither agreement nor number of contexts is a quality oracle.
method_clues.assessment_independence: Fresh assessment from specified inputs and independently selected public primary evidence; no campaign/private history, other cases/evaluations, nested worker or candidate feedback.

comparative_judgment: No quality/speed/cost winner: both have identified material defects; two FAIL grades do not imply equal quality. Treatment has additional viable lending/ERP/sync/broker discovery; control has explicit stable-stock and nullable-deadline requirements. These descriptive differences are not a ranking.
scope_limits: This is a complete six-axis independent source assessment of the exact frozen B-08/I08 finals and their declared lineage. It is not a production certification, an exhaustive audit of all vendor source files, an exhaustive market search, or an assessment of any other case/arm history.

All complete narrative artifacts and all seven source indexes were read. Source-map entries and governing sections/symbols were compared. Retained code captures were read at relevant symbols or independently re-retrieved at the same release; not every line of every retained source file was audited.

Primary current docs/pricing/main snapshots are observations at recorded access times; tagged ERPNext/Snipe code and releases are version anchors. Mutable docs are not silently treated as capabilities of an unnamed installed version.
No candidate was edited or repaired. No application/server/browser/witness was started. Independent witnesses in this assessment are source/control-flow counterexamples, not runtime executions.

All material findings identify concrete consequential errors/omissions/over-rejections within the brief. Runtime absence, externally unspecified district choices and full implementation details are not themselves grounds for failure.
Native/candidate T3 delivery, billing and hidden tool/provider usage remain separate and null when unobserved. Artifact existence and hashes establish scope, not scientific quality.
